criterion.rule: |a - b| <= REL_TOL * max(|a|, |b|, S); S = the estimate's point value (for a comparison's difference also both groups' values); every other field exactly equal

body.justification: The identity of a data build (`<release>:serving-<build_id>:<hash>` on the serving DB, `<release>:load-...` or the legacy `<release>:run<id>:...` on the full DB). It differs between every two databases by design and is not a statistic (docs/operations.md, equivalence criterion, 'What it does not cover'). No response body carries it today; the rule keeps the harness valid if /meta starts to.
sha256 of operation + canonical spec + analytics version + data version: it differs exactly when data_version does. Sent as the X-Analysis-Key header, not in bodies, today.

headers.x-data-version: data build identity (see the data_version rule); checked instead against the version each server reported at start
headers.x-analysis-key: hash including the data version (see the analysis_key rule)
headers.x-cache: cache state (hit/miss/join) depends on request order, not on data
headers.content-length: follows the body, which is compared itself

not_whitelisted./meta data.last_ingested_at, data.ingest: Ingestion provenance. The serving builder copies the source run's id, release and finish time into the serving DB's ingestion_runs row (ADR-013; only data_version and notes are new), so full and serving answer the same. A builder that stopped doing so is caught here, and a rule must then be added deliberately.
not_whitelisted./meta data.respondents, data.years: Facts about the served data: equal by construction of the serving DB.

intended_differences.description: 422/400 `details.errors` are capped at 20 entries with truncated strings (`details.truncated`/`error_count` added). Recognized only when Phase 5's own capping function applied to the baseline's details reproduces Phase 5's details exactly; code and message must be identical.
`activity.preset` longer than 64 characters is now a schema violation (422 `validation_error`, type `string_too_long`) instead of reaching the engine; the baseline also answered 422.
Request bodies over ATUS_API_MAX_BODY_BYTES (65,536 B by default) are refused with 413 `payload_too_large` before parsing.
A POST whose Content-Type is not application/json gets 415 `unsupported_media_type`.
A body FastAPI's JSON parser gave up on (e.g. nested too deeply) is 400 `malformed_json` instead of the generic `http_400`.
Control characters in query parameters are refused with 422 `validation_error` (the baseline let a NUL reach PostgreSQL: 500).
`activity_not_found` names the loaded release's lexicon as 'the <span> activity lexicon' (release-neutral text); code and details unchanged.
GET /health also reports `build`, which the deploy workflow polls.
